summary: Parintins Airport (PIN/SWPI) is a small regional airport serving the city of Parintins in the Amazonas state of northern Brazil. Located on an island in the Amazon River, the airport provides vital air connectivity for residents and visitors traveling to this remote Amazonian community, most famous for hosting the annual Festival de Parintins (Boi-Bumbá). The facility handles primarily domestic regional flights and plays an essential role in connecting the region to Manaus and other Amazonian hubs.
faqs:
Q: What is the main airport serving Parintins, Brazil?
A: Parintins Airport (PIN/SWPI) is the main airport serving the city of Parintins, located in the Amazonas state of Brazil.

Q: Are there direct flights from Parintins to Manaus?
A: Yes, regional carriers operate short flights between Parintins and Eduardo Gomes International Airport in Manaus, the capital of Amazonas state.

Q: When is the busiest time at Parintins Airport?
A: The airport sees its highest traffic during the Festival de Parintins (Boi-Bumbá), a major cultural event held annually in late June, when thousands of visitors arrive to watch the competition between the Garantido and Caprichoso groups.

Q: How large is Parintins Airport?
A: It is classified as a small regional airport with limited infrastructure, serving primarily domestic flights within the Amazon region.
transport_tips: Taxis and motorcycle taxis (mototaxis) are commonly available outside the terminal for short trips into central Parintins, which is only a few kilometers from the airport. During the Boi-Bumbá festival, expect longer waits and surge pricing for ground transportation. Booking accommodations and transport well in advance is strongly recommended if traveling during festival season.
local_tip: Pack light, breathable clothing and rain gear even outside the wet season—Parintins has a hot, humid equatorial climate year-round, and sudden tropical showers are common.
